methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 215 VHR/regional prostate cancer patients (2006-2022) treated with HDR-BT plus EBRT. Appropriate statistical methods: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, univariate and multivariate Cox regression with p<0.1 variable selection for multivariate model. Log-rank testing performed; hazard ratios with 95% CIs reported. However, retrospective design with potential selection bias; treatment protocols evolved over 16-year study period (three different regimens with varying biologically effective doses); no randomization; single surgeon/limited surgeon experience not fully quantified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) of HDR-brachytherapy efficacy in NCCN-defined VHR and regional prostate cancer. High clinical relevance: directly addresses treatment outcomes for aggressive disease phenotype at most treatment centers. 5-year RFS 92.5% and CSS 98.9% represent favorable disease control. However, study demonstrates efficacy in specific institutional context; generalizability to other centers with different expertise limited; no direct comparative data against alternative modalities provided.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods adequately described including treatment protocols (HDR-BT regimens specified with fractionation and doses), EBRT technique (IMRT/VMAT in prone position), and ADT schema. Patient inclusion/exclusion criteria clearly delineated; clinical staging and risk stratification using updated NCCN criteria explicitly stated. Results presentation includes survival curves and statistical comparisons. However, no formal reporting standard referenced (neither STROBE nor REMARK). No data availability statement; statistical code not shared. Heterogeneity in protocols acknowledged but not comprehensively tabulated.

novelty_literature.justification: First study specifically evaluating HDR-BT outcomes exclusively in NCCN-defined VHR category (updated 2023 definition); prior work included heterogeneous high-risk patients under older criteria. HDR-BT technique established; EBRT and ADT standard; combined approach not novel per se. Main contribution: outcome documentation in newly defined aggressive subset; prognostic factor identification (pre-RT PSA, T stage). Mechanistic understanding unchanged; incremental refinement rather than breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript clearly motivating the need to evaluate outcomes in newly defined VHR category. Methods logically presented with comprehensive description of three treatment protocols and evolution over time. Results systematically reported with baseline characteristics, survival curves stratified by clinical parameters, and univariate/multivariate analyses. Discussion appropriately contextualizes within broader literature, acknowledges limitations (retrospective single-center, operator dependence, stage migration from evolving imaging), and proposes future directions including prospective studies with modern imaging (PSMA-PET) and systemic intensification trials.

key_strengths: Substantial cohort (n=215) with long median follow-up (5.6 years) specifically focused on updated NCCN VHR definition, addressing knowledge gap for newly defined aggressive phenotype
Favorable and durable oncologic outcomes (5-year RFS 92.5%, CSS 98.9%, OS 96.2%; 8-year rates 88.5%, 97.8%, 90.8%) demonstrating HDR-BT efficacy
Identified independent prognostic factors (pre-RT PSA >0.1 ng/mL, cT4 stage) enabling risk stratification for potential intensification strategies
Low toxicity profile (Grade ≥3 GU toxicity 1.9%, no Grade ≥3 GI toxicity) supports safety and tolerability of this dose-intense approach
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with potential selection bias; exclusively Japanese cohort limits generalizability; no comparison with alternative modalities (RP, SBRT alone)
Treatment protocol heterogeneity over 16-year period with three different regimens; stage migration from evolving imaging practices; lack of uniform PSMA-PET staging
Operator-dependent procedure; results heavily influenced by institutional expertise and multidisciplinary team; scalability to other centers uncertain
Low event rates (8.8% recurrence, 10.2% mortality) may limit statistical power of Cox models; relatively small number of PC-specific deaths (n=4) limits OS analysis relevance
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid Tier 3 study appropriate for specialist urology/radiation oncology journal. Focuses on well-defined patient population with appropriate outcome metrics and meaningful follow-up. Single-center and retrospective limitations prevent higher tier. Results support HDR-BT's role in multimodality VHR/regional PC management.
